name: Tramadol
drug_class: Atypical centrally acting opioid analgesic with serotonin–noradrenaline reuptake inhibition
route_note: Mainly oral capsules and immediate- or extended-release tablets; injections and suppositories in some countries.

discovery.note: Synthesised in 1962 and launched in West Germany in 1977.

rx_status: controlled (US Schedule IV; UK Class C, Schedule 3)
tagline: Dual-action opioid and monoamine reuptake inhibitor for moderate pain
summary: Tramadol is a synthetic analgesic combining weak mu-opioid agonism, mainly through its metabolite O-desmethyltramadol, with serotonin and noradrenaline reuptake inhibition. Once marketed as low-risk, it is now controlled in many countries and associated with seizures, serotonin syndrome and widespread non-medical use in parts of Africa and the Middle East.
mechanism: Tramadol is a racemic mixture. The (+)-enantiomer inhibits serotonin reuptake and is converted by CYP2D6 to (+)-O-desmethyltramadol (M1), a mu-opioid agonist far more potent than the parent; the (−)-enantiomer inhibits noradrenaline reuptake.

Monoaminergic actions enhance descending inhibitory pain pathways. The dependence on CYP2D6 means variable opioid effect, and serotonergic activity explains risks of serotonin syndrome and lowered seizure threshold.

history.title: German launch
history.detail: Tramadol is marketed in West Germany as Tramal.

history.title: US approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Ultram (Ortho-McNeil) as an unscheduled analgesic.

history.title: US scheduling
history.detail: The DEA places tramadol in Schedule IV; the UK makes it a Class C controlled drug the same year.

history.title: Paediatric contraindication
history.detail: The FDA contraindicates tramadol in children under 12 and after tonsillectomy under 18.

history.title: Illicit trafficking concerns
history.detail: The UN Office on Drugs and Crime reports large seizures of high-strength tramadol in West Africa and the Middle East.

pk.metabolism: hepatic: CYP2D6 to active M1, CYP3A4 and CYP2B6 to N-desmethyltramadol

serious: Respiratory depression (especially in CYP2D6 ultrarapid metabolisers)
safety.boxed_warning: Addiction, abuse and misuse; life-threatening respiratory depression; accidental exposure; neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome; CYP3A4 interactions; risks with benzodiazepines or other CNS depressants (US opioid class boxed warning). Ultrarapid metabolism of tramadol and life-threatening respiratory depression in children.

facts: Tramadol is not under international control by the UN conventions, which has allowed large unregulated markets in some regions.
